aboutGame.title: What Is Tribes 3v3?
paragraphs: Tribes 3v3 is a small-team competitive shooter built around three-player squads fighting fast, objective-driven rounds. With no fourth teammate to cover a bad angle, every duel, route, and ability decision swings the round, which is why positioning, crosshair placement, and coordination matter far more than raw flick speed.

The Tribes 3v3 Wiki turns that pressure into practical guides: class and role archetypes, weapon and loadout picks, keybinds and camera settings, the shard and upgrade economy, plus mode-specific tactics for 3v3, rivals, tournaments, and private lobbies.

modules.name: Tribes 3v3 Beginner Guide
modules.description: The core fundamentals for new players: where you stand, where your crosshair sits, and when you commit to a fight.

highlights.detail: Keep cover between you and the enemy and never stand in the same open lane twice.
Fix your setup once: tune camera and aim sensitivity, then leave it alone so your aim stays consistent.
Build one reliable loadout and learn its limits before you experiment with new kits.
Play with the team: move with at least one teammate and focus the same target.
Review each engagement and ask what caused the exchange to succeed or fail.
Fix one recurring mistake per session instead of chasing five small ones at once.

modules.name: Tribes 3v3 Classes
modules.description: How the ranged, entry, and flex archetypes split responsibility, and which three-player combinations hold up in a round.

highlights.label: Ranged
highlights.detail: Holds sightlines and punishes open pushes, and is strongest on long lanes and elevated ground.

highlights.label: Entry
highlights.detail: Breaks corners and forces tight duels, but is exposed the moment the fight opens up.

highlights.label: Flex
highlights.detail: Fills whatever the squad is missing and adapts once the first engagement shows the enemy plan.

highlights.label: Comps
highlights.detail: Aggressive push, defensive hold, and balanced setups, with balanced as the default for new squads.

modules.name: Tribes 3v3 Weapons
modules.description: Weapon archetypes by range, and the squad role each one actually fits in a three-player fight.

highlights.label: Close
highlights.detail: Fast-firing picks that win point-blank trades and punish corners, but fall apart across open ground.

highlights.label: Mid
highlights.detail: All-rounders that stay flexible at most distances and are the default pick for newer squads.

highlights.label: Long
highlights.detail: Precision picks that punish anyone holding an open lane, but get collapsed on by close-range pushes.

highlights.label: Utility
highlights.detail: Secondaries that finish weakened targets and cover reload gaps without carrying a fight alone.

modules.name: Tribes 3v3 Movement
modules.description: Movement, camera, and input settings that keep your aim predictable once the fight starts.

highlights.detail: Learn the default layout first: keep the movement keys familiar, use Spacebar to reposition, and leave the mouse for camera and aim.
Strafe with the left and right keys instead of backpedaling, so your crosshair stays on the fight.
Start on default camera sensitivity and change one value at a time across a full session.
Match aim sensitivity to camera sensitivity so fine tracking stays consistent.
Keep mouse DPI on one constant value, then stop touching it.
Rebind abilities to keys your fingers already rest near, then confirm them in the in-game control display.

modules.name: Tribes 3v3 Maps
modules.description: Battlefield reading: corners, side routes, elevated ground, and long sightlines that decide who controls the round.

highlights.label: Corners
highlights.detail: Narrow entrances hide ambushes, so clear them methodically and expect close-range fights.

highlights.label: Routes
highlights.detail: Split across side routes to create crossfire from two angles instead of one.

highlights.label: Elevation
highlights.detail: Take elevated ground early and use it to reposition or hold overwatch.

highlights.label: Sightlines
highlights.detail: Break line of sight on long lanes and rotate out rather than trading at range.

highlights.label: Crossfire
highlights.detail: Cover the same doorway from two angles with enough spacing that one ability cannot remove both of you.

highlights.label: 3v3
highlights.detail: Three players per side, short rounds, and no spare teammate, so every death is a tempo swing.

highlights.label: Rivals
highlights.detail: Repeat matchups against familiar squads, where scouting routes beats forcing early fights.

highlights.label: Tournament
highlights.detail: Bracket play built on trio roles, loadout synergies, and map control under pressure.

highlights.label: Private
highlights.detail: Private lobbies for scrims, route walkthroughs, and repeatable practice reps.

modules.name: Tribes 3v3 Tips
modules.description: The improvement tips that actually move your win rate, ranked by how much they matter.

highlights.label: S
highlights.detail: Positioning: cover usage and repositioning after damage decide who gets the first shot.

highlights.label: S
highlights.detail: Crosshair placement: pre-aim entry points instead of flicking across the screen.

highlights.label: A
highlights.detail: Duel discipline: back off from low-percentage fights instead of forcing a shot after a miss.

highlights.label: B
highlights.detail: Movement: strafe during combat, because standing still loses even trades.

faq.title: Tribes 3v3 FAQ
faq.description: Quick answers to the questions new Tribes 3v3 players ask most.

items.question: What is Tribes 3v3?
items.answer: Tribes 3v3 is a small-team competitive shooter where three-player squads fight fast, objective-driven rounds. Because only three players take the field per side, positioning, ability timing, and communication decide most rounds, not raw aim.

items.question: Which class should beginners pick in Tribes 3v3?
items.answer: Start with a balanced composition: one ranged overwatch player, one close-range entry player, and one flex player. Balanced setups adapt to both offense and defense and are the default recommendation for new squads.

items.question: How do shards work in Tribes 3v3?
items.answer: Shards are the in-round resource layer behind your abilities and loadout choices. Spend them on planned entries, real escapes, and confirmed eliminations, and avoid dumping everything on first contact.

items.question: What are the most important skills in Tribes 3v3?
items.answer: Positioning and crosshair placement carry the most weight, followed by duel discipline and ability timing. Consistency beats flash, so take fights you can actually win instead of chasing highlight shots.

items.question: How do I improve faster in Tribes 3v3?
items.answer: Fix your setup once, lock in a single reliable loadout, play with at least one teammate, review each engagement, and fix one recurring mistake per session.

items.question: What is the fastest way to get shards in Tribes 3v3?
items.answer: Shard income comes from how you play the round, so the fastest gains come from winning engagements cleanly: keep cover, focus the same target as a teammate, and stop spending on low-value fights.
